title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
body_text:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available. AgentCore is an agentic platform for building, deploying, and operating AI agents securely at scale, using any framework and any foundation model, in or outside of Amazon Bedrock.

AgentCore services include Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Browser, Code Interpreter, and Observability. You can use each service on its own or combine them. AgentCore works with the open source frameworks you already use, including CrewAI, Google ADK, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Strands Agents.

AgentCore Runtime provides complete session isolation and supports long-running workloads of up to 8 hours. At general availability, AgentCore adds support for Amazon VPC, AWS PrivateLink, AWS CloudFormation, and resource tagging, and Runtime supports the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. AgentCore Observability delivers OpenTelemetry-compatible telemetry through Amazon CloudWatch so you can trace each step an agent takes.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is available in nine AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (Ireland).

title: Amazon Aurora DSQL
body_text:
Amazon Aurora DSQL is the fastest serverless distributed SQL database for always available applications. Aurora DSQL is PostgreSQL-compatible, so you can build with the drivers, object-relational mapping frameworks, and SQL features you already know.

Aurora DSQL offers active-active high availability, with 99.99% availability in single-Region configurations and 99.999% availability in multi-Region configurations. Multi-Region clusters provide strong consistency, so reads and writes to any Regional endpoint of a multi-Region cluster always return the latest committed data.

Aurora DSQL scales reads, writes, compute, and storage independently to meet any workload demand, with no infrastructure to provision, patch, or upgrade. At general availability, Aurora DSQL also supports AWS Backup, AWS PrivateLink, and AWS CloudFormation.

Amazon Aurora DSQL is generally available in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), and Europe (Paris).

title: Amazon Q Developer Pricing
body_text:
Amazon Q Developer offers a Free Tier and a Pro Tier. The Free Tier is available to individual developers with an AWS Builder ID or through the AWS Management Console. It includes a monthly allowance of agentic chat interactions in the IDE and command line, and lets you transform up to 1,000 lines of code per month.

The Amazon Q Developer Pro Tier is $19 per month per user. The Pro Tier includes higher usage limits, user and policy management through AWS IAM Identity Center, and the ability for administrators to manage subscriptions for their organization.

With the Pro Tier, code transformation includes 4,000 lines of code per month per user, pooled at the account level. Lines of code submitted beyond the pooled allowance are charged at $0.003 per line of code.

Prices are in USD and do not include applicable taxes. Subscriptions are billed monthly to your AWS account.

title: Amazon S3 Vectors
body_text:
Amazon S3 Vectors is the first cloud object store with native support to store and query vectors, delivering purpose-built, cost-optimized vector storage for AI agents, AI inference, and semantic search. S3 Vectors can reduce the total cost of uploading, storing, and querying vectors by up to 90%.

S3 Vectors introduces vector buckets, a new bucket type with a dedicated set of APIs to store, access, and query vector data without provisioning any infrastructure. Each vector bucket can have up to 10,000 vector indexes, and each index can hold tens of millions of vectors. You can attach metadata as key-value pairs to each vector to filter queries.

S3 Vectors integrates natively with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, and works with Amazon OpenSearch Service so you can keep infrequently queried vectors in S3 and move frequently queried vectors to OpenSearch for low-latency search.

Amazon S3 Vectors is available in preview in the US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), and Asia Pacific (Sydney) Regions.

title: Accelerate safe software releases with new built-in blue/green deployments in Amazon ECS
body_text:
Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) now includes built-in support for blue/green deployments, making it safer and more consistent to release new versions of your containerized applications without building custom deployment tooling.

With a blue/green deployment, Amazon ECS creates the new green revision of your service alongside the existing blue revision, shifts production traffic to green, and keeps blue running during a bake time you configure. If something goes wrong, you can roll back to the blue revision without downtime.

You can use deployment lifecycle hooks to run AWS Lambda functions at specific stages of the deployment, for example to run validation tests against the green revision before production traffic shifts to it.

Built-in blue/green deployments are available today in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon ECS is available, at no additional charge.

title: AWS Lambda increases maximum payload size from 256 KB to 1 MB for asynchronous invocations
body_text:
AWS Lambda increases the maximum payload size for asynchronous invocations from 256 KB to 1 MB. You can now send larger payloads to Lambda functions invoked asynchronously, including through the Lambda Invoke API and event sources that invoke functions asynchronously such as Amazon EventBridge and Amazon SNS.

Previously, customers with payloads larger than 256 KB had to split them into chunks or store them in Amazon S3 and pass a reference to the function. With this change, you can pass richer event data directly, which simplifies event-driven architectures.

Asynchronous invocations with payloads above 256 KB are billed as one request for each 64 KB chunk of the payload. This increase is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS Lambda is available.

title: Amazon Quick Suite
body_text:
Amazon Quick Suite is now generally available, giving business users one agentic workspace for research, business intelligence and workflow automation. Quick Suite is an agentic teammate that answers questions at work and turns the answers into actions, without switching between tools.

Quick Suite includes Quick Research for in-depth research across company data and trusted outside sources, Quick Sight for business intelligence dashboards and plain-language questions, Quick Flows for automating everyday tasks, and Quick Automate for multi-step business processes. Quick Index connects your documents and data so Quick Suite can find answers in them.

title: Anthropic's Claude in Amazon Bedrock
body_text:
Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.5 is now available in Amazon Bedrock, with support for long-running agent tasks and complex coding workloads for enterprise builders. Claude Sonnet 4.5 can keep working through multi-step tasks and large codebases, which suits teams automating software development and business workflows.

You can call Claude Sonnet 4.5 through the Amazon Bedrock API, and build and run agents with it using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Amazon Bedrock also offers other Claude models, so teams can pick the model that fits each workload's speed and cost.

title: AWS Free Tier
body_text: Starting July 15, 2025, new AWS customers receive $100 in AWS Free Tier credits at sign-up and can earn up to $100 more by exploring key AWS services. Customers earn the extra credits by completing activities with services such as Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, AWS Lambda, Amazon Bedrock and AWS Budgets.
